content.title: Recommendations for acute-phase treatment of high-risk pulmonary embolism

recommendations.text: It is recommended that anticoagulation with UFH, including a weight-adjusted bolus injection, be initiated without delay in patients with high-risk PE.
recommendations.notes: Immediate anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin for high-risk PE.

recommendations.text: Systemic thrombolytic therapy is recommended for high-risk PE.
recommendations.notes: Thrombolysis as first-line reperfusion therapy for high-risk pulmonary embolism.

recommendations.text: Surgical pulmonary embolectomy is recommended for patients with high-risk PE, in whom thrombolysis is contraindicated or has failed.
recommendations.notes: Surgical embolectomy when thrombolysis not possible or unsuccessful (footnote: if appropriate expertise and resources are available on-site).

recommendations.text: Percutaneous catheter-directed treatment should be considered for patients with high-risk PE, in whom thrombolysis is contraindicated or has failed.
recommendations.notes: Endovascular catheter-directed approaches as an alternative when thrombolysis is not an option or failed.

recommendations.text: Norepinephrine and/or dobutamine should be considered in patients with high-risk PE.
recommendations.notes: Vasoactive support for haemodynamic compromise in high-risk PE.

recommendations.text: ECMO may be considered, in combination with surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed treatment, in patients with PE and refractory circulatory collapse or cardiac arrest.
recommendations.notes: Extracorporeal support as rescue therapy in refractory circulatory collapse or cardiac arrest.

footnotes_and_references.a: See Table 4 for definition of high-risk PE. After haemodynamic stabilization of the patient, continue with anticoagulation treatment as in intermediate- or low-risk PE (section 6.7).
footnotes_and_references.d: If appropriate expertise and resources are available on-site.
